title: Grand Guignol
subtitle: Horror! Gore! A play where both the actors and the audience pass out by the end—that's what makes a truly great performance!

trails.title: Depths of Myth
trails.description: A round of applause for the latest research breakthrough—don't forget to raise a toast!

content.text:
Everything is unfolding right now.
No form of divination, prophecy, thought, or those feelings of déjà vu and dreams is just a coincidence.
Imagine a vault that exists beyond both time and space. Inside it lies everything. Love and hatred, good luck and bad luck, the oldest archetypes and legends. Under normal circumstances, we could never reach it. But the Guiding One and the "Storm" have made this miracle possible. Now, the Archive of Imagery, known as the "Depths of Myth," has become visible to us.
We owe a great deal to the pioneer whose research and courage made this possible. Her dedication and sacrifice deserve our deepest respect. We would all be wise to follow her example.
...

items.text: A fine restaurant that requires reservations may not be an ideal spot for dinner after an adventure.
The atmosphere brooks no laughter, no clinking glasses—just conversation restrained under the weight of etiquette.
The room hums with quiet small talk pierced by the faint scraping of silver over porcelain.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You cannot cut steak with a necklace in your hand, Adèle. Why not put it down? Just for a while.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No. Thank you, madame, but I can't afford to lose it again.
She saws through her steak mechanically, arrhythmically, lost in undercooked thought.
The sawing becomes like a chore; she pushes through muscle and sinew until she's all but sawing the plate in half.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Damn! This is practically a tire, not a steak!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Allow me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No. Thank you.
During idle conversation, a diner from the next table steps forward.

items.speaker: Pensive Young Man
items.text: Oh, Madame Bouanich. It's been a long time. I'm glad to see that you're still in Paris.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: And you? Still in search of your lost fate?

items.speaker: Pensive Young Man
items.text: I ... I'm not sure anymore.

items.speaker: Pensive Young Man
items.text: What you said may have been right: fate is a kind of erratic stream—to search for meaning in it or impose meaning upon it is pointless.

items.speaker: Pensive Young Man
items.text: Even so, some part of me still longs to try. Perhaps it will one day be in reach.

items.speaker: Pensive Young Man
items.text: But I wouldn't want us to dwell on my insignificant problems. I understand that Professor Roseau has made some interesting breakthroughs in the resurrection of the dead.

items.speaker: Pensive Young Man
items.text: Though first, perhaps you'd introduce the lady here?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: She is the one I spoke of before, the girl who stands at the confluence of streams.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Adèle, this is a regular of mine. We call him Hummingbird.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: A pleasure, I'm sure.

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: Ah, yes, I see what she means.

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: You look a little pensive, miss. I wonder have you found yourself seeing otherworldly figures and hearing elusive voices? Are you still yourself?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What are you talking about?
The young man notices Adèle's behavior. A moment later, he returns with new dishes—a bowl of mashed potatoes and a plate of macarons.

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: I'd say you'd prefer these over steak.
She sets down her knife, wavering between the two plates before finally taking the macarons.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: They're passable.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Though nowhere near as good as Ladurée, I must say.
Her words weren't meant as praise, yet she can't help but return to the plate for another.

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: The professor is about to give his speech. If you don't mind, Madame Bouanich, might we continue our chat later?
He returns to his table. Guests around him greet him cordially, giving the whole event a sense of ritual familiarity.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What on earth is Roseau up to?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: He has an announcement to make, one that defines his life's work.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Ah. It seems he's made himself presentable for the occasion.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Greetings, dear brethren. We gather here today to celebrate a momentous discovery.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: One that belongs to arcanists alone. A breakthrough that lies far beyond the reach of human comprehension.

items.speaker: Old Woman
items.text: Enough with the self-aggrandizing. Get to the point.

items.speaker: Old Woman
items.text: I didn't come all this way to watch you pump yourself full of hot air.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: There's no need to rush, is there, Animus? We have all the time we need.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Since the year 1999, our search for the promised land has never ceased.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Following the will of the Guiding One, we have unraveled countless mysteries of the "Storm." For this great cause, many of our noble comrades paid the greatest sacrifice, their souls sowing the seeds of our coming harvest.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Our endeavor was never expected to be easy, but, tell me, has it ever crossed your minds whether the "Storm" is the sole path to the promised land we have collectively sought to bring about?

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Further still, do all of us here, myself included, share in the same vision of that world? We are nothing like the Foundation's numb, obedient lapdogs incapable of independent thought, wouldn't you agree?

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: The "Storm" promises only a change to our imperfect, superficial world. Yet I believe a transcendent world may be drawn up from the Depths of Myth—a world where each and every dream becomes reality. Tell me, which would you prefer?

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Same old song and dance.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Perhaps you'd care to show something new and actually feasible, for once? Otherwise, you'll get naught from me.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: My dear Animus. Worry not, for I have come well-prepared to open your eyes.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: I have discovered a means to access the Depths of Myth, and, through it, achieved a miracle—the miracle of resurrection! Allow me to demonstrate.
The professor walks toward a corner of the banquet hall, holding rapt attention from the gathered diners.
Her right hand, presently reaching for another macaron, stops mid-motion, deftly, automatically, switching to pick up a napkin instead.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: When one's flesh and spirit are fully immersed in the Depths of Myth, their body frays and sinks until, eventually, it disintegrates.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Yet the spirit remains intact. For in that realm, the spirit is itself the most authentic and pristine substance.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Reality as we know it is nothing more than a crude layer of degraded substance laid over the Depths of Myth. And so long as one's consciousness remains within its maelstrom, that person may be raised from it again!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Our Félicienne here is the very proof that the mind alone may be brought back to physical reality! Though she perished, she now sits before us once more.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: So, one and all, let us raise a toast to her revival!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Roseau? What in heaven's name are you trying to say?
She sets down her napkin and rises from her seat.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Ah, Félicienne, you've fully rejoined us now, haven't you? Won't you please introduce yourself?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What do you expect me to say? You know very well who I am.
The diviner's eyes follow her, though the focus of her vision lies far beyond this hall.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: How are you feeling?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I would feel a great deal better without your patronizing tone, madame. I have neither need nor want of your sympathy.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ahem.
She lifts a glass of red wine to her chest.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: And here, before you now is Félicienne, Priestess of Lightning, advisor to the Sun King, vassal of the Guiding One.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Attend to my words: I have conquered fate and overcome death itself to stand here!

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: I arose from the Depths of Myth by my own power, unlike the poor, unworthy fools Roseau sent in.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Yet he dares to claim this miraculous deed for his own. What a disgrace, sir. Have you no shame?

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: But of course, you don't. All of you nonentities lack in both gratitude and shame. Basking in the grace of the Guiding One and myself, without even realizing it.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Did you think you had even scratched the surface of the power that dwells here? Roseau—you utter fool, this affront of yours ought to cost you your life.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Yet, I am not so base as to destroy what may still have use. So, just this once, I will forgive you.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: As for the rest of you, my forgiveness likewise extends to the rudeness you all showed in stuffing your faces before toasting to my health.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Now, to my health!

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: This is a miracle!

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: Bringing the dead back to life—it isn't really possible, is it?

items.speaker: Giant Puppet
items.text: She came back to life? So we can't die anymore, like what the Guiding One said?

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Pah. What a farce.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: All you've done is manipulated some girl into believing she's Félicienne, and yet you dare to call it a "miraculous resurrection."

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: What utter blasphemy! An offense to the word "miracle" and to the Guiding One Herself!

items.speaker: Petite Girl
items.text: I heard another voice in Félicienne, one that belongs to someone else. Could that mean ...?

items.speaker: Distant Lady
items.text: Why do we speak as if she is not present? Let us bring our concerns to her.

items.speaker: Distant Lady
items.text: There are things only the true Félicienne would know.

items.speaker: Crab-Faced Man
items.text: Mind alone returning to reality? But has Félicienne lost her arcane skills in the process? If so, then this revival is meaningless.

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: Whatever the case may be, if this is a true venue of life eternal, should we not seize it? At least until we find an alchemist capable of concocting the Fountain of Youth.

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: I believe I see one drawback already. Only one who dies in the Depths of Myth may be returned from it. To die elsewhere would be to lose the original image of one's being.

items.speaker: Hummingbird
items.text: I imagine this is our shared goal then—to unleash the Depths of Myth upon the material world so that we might render a collective image of all who dwell in this era to be raised anew.
A demure and polite voice in the corner interrupts their debate.

items.speaker: Portrait of a Woman
items.text: But ought we not to first celebrate Félicienne's return?

items.speaker: Portrait of a Woman
items.text: Though, I must say it is a strange sort of return. How different she looks, doesn't she?

items.speaker: Crab-Faced Man
items.text: True. This dowdy girl is a poor vessel for one so noble.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Mind your tongues. You're speaking of my new body here.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: For all her faults, I would not call the girl "dowdy." She simply chose to turn a blind eye to beauty. I've always felt she picked the wrong career.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: I admit it did her some good. She learned to read people and how to put them at ease.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: But it pulled her further from her true heritage and from the refined taste expected of a jewel hunter.

items.speaker: Portrait of a Woman
items.text: So, Félicienne, your right hand—is it alright?

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Whatever do you mean?

items.speaker: Portrait of a Woman
items.text: Do you not feel it trembling? Damn! Is something wrong?!
Her right hand moves on its own, splashing the wine across her face before she can stop it.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Uggh! Adèle, you insolent ...!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: *deep breath*
It's like being shocked awake by cold water. Her eyes freeze open as she scans the room.
Around her sits a gawking zoo of monsters and aberrations, and she's the exhibit.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You're Manus Vindictae! Why did you bring me here? What are you doing to me?
Realization hits. Panic tightens in her chest; she clutches the diamond in her hand. Trickles of blood and wine seep through her fingers.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Stop! I will not accept any damage to my body, Ustrina! Nor from you, Lyra!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: One move and I'll burn you to a crisp, inside and out!

items.speaker: Portrait of a Woman
items.text: What's happened, Félicienne? It is only us. We're still here at the banquet thrown in your honor.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Stop your prattling, you rubbish dump! Another word and I'll rip that canvas to shreds!

items.speaker: Portrait of a Woman
items.text: *sniff*

items.speaker: Giant Puppet
items.text: She's so angry. That means she has to really be Félicienne.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Words of wisdom from a puppet of all things. Need I point out who pulls your strings, Hypothetik?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You cowards, ganging up on a poor innocent woman! Each and every one of you is a monster! I won't play whatever game you have in store for me!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Get out of my way!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Fascinating. Though Félicienne's spirit has seized control of her body, the former spirit seems able to resist.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: If I am indeed correct, what we are seeing is their thoughts and memories beginning to blend, causing this confusion.
The professor scribbles down notes in a rapturous flurry, recording every little tic, word, and movement.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Laurent Roseau, you've been in league with Manus Vindictae all along! You were lying to me! Everything Célia said was true!
Adèle attempts a show of defiance, but all she receives in return are curious, observant stares.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: My dear, no one here has mentioned Manus Vindictae but you.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Yet you seem to know a great deal about those present already.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Far too much to be a mere guess. You have met these people before.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I won't let you play with my mind again, Beryl. Célia told me all about these thugs. She told me everything!
Then it dawns on her. A flaw in her own reasoning.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Maybe not exactly everything. But she did tell me that it was Manus Vindictae that killed her!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Roseau! Félicienne! You killed her! You-You murderous Manus scum!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I believe it is time you faced the truth.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The "truth"? What is it this time? You think I don't see through you?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You killed Célia.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: In that place where the Archive of Imagery overlapped with reality, you killed her by your own hand.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wh-What?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You remember it, do you not? You allowed it to happen.
She searches for any sort of proof she might have to match her claims.
She should never have listened to these lunatics. Maybe she should've just torn them apart with her bare hands.
Start with that woman. Tear open a path, get back to the car, drive off, and then ...
The banquet ends in chaos, though the guests hardly seem to take notice or seem to even care. A small band of waiters arrives to begin clearing the scene.
The professor steps over the shards of glass and porcelain to where Beryl sits.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Félicienne has quite the flair for the dramatics, doesn't she? And as always, our audience simply sat back, their eyes glued and mouths agape.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: We are indeed fortunate for your skill in divination.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: We will have to wait for Félicienne to return to her senses, but thereafter we follow the plan as discussed:

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Using the French Blue as our focal point, we will draw up the true, perfect Paris from the Depths of Myth.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Democratic, independent, chosen by her people, and shaped by the dreams of every one of her citizens.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I have seen many versions of Paris, from flames to paradise. Nothing is beyond possibility.
Beryl offers a vague, distant reply; she looks out toward the open doors but says nothing more.
The professor holds his stare on the pendulum in Beryl's hand, guessing she's once again trapped in a trance, and leaves her be.
Prophecy is something to be revered and feared.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: So, tomorrow at dawn, we will perform the final ritual atop the Eiffel Tower.
